R6-18_phrase_carries_assertion.rule: The quoted phrase must itself carry the assertion; context may clarify subject or sense but may not supply the assertion. Step A counts existing outside-formula rescues with no model calls, and stops for the author if more than 10 card accepts rely on them or any public-certified cell would lose its last citation. Step B: gate6-v1.6 replaces the outside-formula permission with the verbatim text, plus a code guard refusing asserted_outside_formula = Y accepts. The inference line moves to gate6-v1.7.
R6-18_phrase_carries_assertion.verbatim_text: THE PHRASE CARRIES THE ASSERTION. The quoted phrase must itself assert the property of the required subject. Surrounding text may establish who the subject is or what the quoted words mean, but it may not supply an assertion the quoted words do not make. If the passage asserts the property only in a different sentence, the citation does not satisfy the family (BELOW_FLOOR); that other sentence is the one to cite.
R6-18_phrase_carries_assertion.removed_from_v15: unless the passage separately asserts the predicate outside the formula.
